title: Eval-contracts and stochastic rollback orchestrator
creator: Asha Patel
description: Introduce an orchestration layer that enforces lightweight, testable 'eval contracts' for canary and A/B rollouts and uses a stochastic rollback policy to reduce noisy false positives. Eval contracts are compact specifications for a small set of signature prompts (anchor probes) describing expected score distributions, categorical behavior assertions, and per-probe tolerance windows. This ticket implements the controller, integrates it with shadow traffic, and wires signals into the rollout engine for probabilistic rollback decisions.
goals: Define a machine-readable eval contract schema that fits in rollout configs
Implement a controller that evaluates incoming probe streams (shadow + canary) against contracts in near-real-time
Add a stochastic rollback policy that converts multi-probe signals into an actionable rollback probability instead of deterministic flip-flops
Expose per-probe and aggregate visualizations in the Console and emit structured events for audits and incident playbooks
decisions: We will avoid a strict per-probe threshold gating approach because it produces frequent noisy rollbacks for low-frequency probes. Instead we adopt small-n statistical priors (Bayesian posterior on per-probe deltas) and a calibrated conversion to a rollback probability. We also standardize on a compact JSON schema for eval contracts to allow reuse across customers and per-team overrides. Trade-offs: increased controller complexity and a need for simulated canary traffic for calibration, versus better stability and fewer mistaken rollbacks in production.
plan: Design eval contract schema and version it (confluence: /r/confluence/eval-contracts-v1)
Implement probe ingestion pipeline that tags anchor probe responses from shadow and canary traffic
Build statistical evaluator service: per-probe Bayesian comparator + aggregate risk model
Integrate rollback signal into rollout conductor with a tunable 'rollback probability -> action' mapping
Add Console dashboards: per-probe score bands, posterior distributions, and a simulated canary replay tool
Create unit/integration tests and a canary-simulation harness to validate false positive rates
updates: 2025-02-15: Kickoff - scoped to host-side evaluation only (no on-prem agent yet). Agreed to keep contract schema minimal: id, description, metric, expected_distribution, tolerance_window.
2025-02-20: PoC ingestion: shadow tagging implemented in runtime (PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pulls/3897). Initial probe throughput shows <2% overhead on p95 latency when sampling at 1%.

2025-02-25: Design review with PM and DX. Decision to use Bayesian shrinkage priors to stabilize low-count probes. UX mockups for per-probe visualization uploaded (drive:/design/eval-contracts/ux-v1).

2025-03-02: First integration test passed. Stochastic rollback converter validated in simulator against historical release data (replay of last 12 months): false positive rate reduced by ~60% compared to rule-based gating.

2025-03-02: Blocker discovered: current rollout conductor API expects deterministic boolean signals. Need a small API extension to accept 'rollback_score' (0.0-1.0) and a mapping config. Filed ENG-90711 as dependency.
acceptance_criteria: Eval contract schema v1 documented and stored in Confluence
Controller can ingest and evaluate anchor probes from shadow and canary traffic with <250ms median added latency
Stochastic rollback score is emitted to rollout conductor API and the conductor responds according to mapping config
Console shows per-probe posterior and an aggregate risk gauge; links to underlying events for audits
Canary-simulation harness demonstrates FP rate <= 0.5% on historical replays while preserving detection of real regressions in at least 90% of injected-failure tests
